title: ArchDoc export
description: A specification repository, the relationships ArchDoc derives from it, and every document as a flat ordered list of its headings. From schema 2 onwards this shape only ever gains optional fields.

commit.description: The revision this export describes, as given to --commit. Absent when it was not given. Taken as written and not checked against a repository.

has_glossary.description: Whether the repository has a glossary page. Present even where glossary is not, so a tree's index.json still answers it.

config.description: Every setting archdoc.json holds. The location it was read from is not among them: it describes the machine that ran the command.

branch.description: The branch frozen documents are compared against.

root.description: Relative to the directory holding archdoc.json.

strict.description: False also permits draft to accepted and draft to rejected.

ref_stale_days.description: How old a ref's verified date may be. 0 disables the check.

id.description: Absent for spec pages, which are named rather than numbered.

page.description: A spec page's path below spec/ without the extension.

status.description: Absent for spec pages and refs, which have no lifecycle.

backfilled.description: The date the document was written to record a decision taken earlier.

included_in.description: Names of the spec pages including this document.

effectively_obsolete.description: An accepted document obsoletes this one.

implemented.description: An accepted RFC or ADR that some spec page other than the glossary includes.

stale.description: A spec page including something effectively obsolete.

required_sections.description: The level two headings this type calls for, in order. Checked by lint rather than guaranteed, so any of them may be missing from contents. A section is that unit and is not the same as a contents entry.

contents.description: Every heading in document order, each with the prose beneath it. Content before the first heading belongs to no entry and appears only in source.

source.description: The file exactly as it is on disk, front matter included. Present only with --source. The one field that reproduces the document.

entry.description: One heading and the lines beneath it, up to the next heading of any level. No entry holds another's prose, so walking them reads every line of a body once.

level.description: Carried rather than implied by nesting, because heading levels need not descend one at a time.

text.description: The heading as written, without its marker.

anchor.description: As GitHub computes it. A repeat within a document gains a numbered suffix. Set your heading ids from this rather than generating your own.

line.description: 1-based in the file. The body begins on the next line, so a position inside it needs no further arithmetic.

body.description: The lines as written, untrimmed. Empty where one heading follows another directly. Absent where bodies were excluded.

text.description: A definition's text is its label.

type.description: inline is [text](destination), image is ![text](destination), definition is [label]: destination. A reference use carries a label rather than a destination and is not listed: rewriting the definition carries its uses.

path.description: Resolved against the repository root. Absent when it leaves the repository.

resolves_to.description: The identifier, or a spec page's name. Absent when the destination is not a document.
